findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is set, so objects (including the seeded vendor-roster.xlsx file) are stored unencrypted at rest by default.

findings.issue_category: no bucket ACL / public access controls
findings.description: No acl attribute or public access block is defined, leaving the bucket to default settings without an explicit private ACL or public-access-block restriction, increasing risk of unintended public exposure.
The bucket stores ledger export data (likely sensitive financial data) but has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving data unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, so model artifacts are stored unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, leaving operational runbook data (which may contain sensitive operational/credential information) unencrypted at rest.

The acl is set to the malformed/non-standard value 'lcatalogopts-delivery-write' instead of a canned ACL like 'log-delivery-write' or 'private'; if Terraform accepts or defaults this incorrectly it could result in unintended (e.g., public or overly broad) access grants on the audit trail bucket, undermining the integrity of audit logs.

findings.issue_category: plaintext sensitive data upload without encryption enforcement
findings.description: The object is uploaded to reports_archive, a bucket without server-side encryption configured, so this vendor roster file (potentially containing sensitive vendor/PII data) is stored unencrypted at rest.
